description: crate-jmap-base-client/src/blob.rs:419-426 builds the hex string with hash.iter().fold(String::with_capacity(64), |mut s, b| { s.push(...); s.push(...); s }) — the fold-with-mut-accumulator pattern that clippy flags under clippy::manual_fold / unused_self_for_fold-style discussions. Iterator::fold is the right tool when you fold to a new value at each step; mutating the accumulator and returning it is a code smell that uses fold's name without its semantics. Idiomatic Rust here is a for loop into a pre-sized String: let mut s = String::with_capacity(64); for b in hash.iter() { s.push(hex_nibble_lower(*b >> 4)); s.push(hex_nibble_lower(*b & 0x0f)); } s. Reads in one direction, no closure noise, same performance. (The alternative — std::fmt::Write — paid format-machinery cost we don't want on the upload hot path, so the for loop is the right destination.) Low priority because it works correctly; flagged because the pattern is copied into every cookie-cutter sibling crate and propagates the wince.
title: compute_sha256_hex uses fold-with-mut-accumulator anti-idiom
